$comment: TrustLens seed corpus v1. EVERY case in this file is SYNTHETIC — authored by the programme for testing. NO case is a real-world sample, and none may be presented as evidence of real scam activity (MP §8, §21). Phone numbers, VPAs, URLs and names are deliberately fictitious. Benign cases were authored FIRST, per CONF-002, because they are the regression tests that prevent the engine degenerating into a keyword matcher.
amended: 2026-08-28 — 3 benign near-misses (B-011..B-013, incl. an adversarial official-educational post) and 3 malicious cases (M-012 boss scam, M-013 crypto wallet drain, M-014 USSD call-forwarding) added for the rules the RESEARCH-006 manual retrieval reconciliation made publishable. All remain SYNTHETIC.
usage_constraints: Supports determinism and regression testing ONLY.
MUST NOT be used to compute or claim precision, recall, or false-positive rate — a synthetic corpus cannot support an accuracy claim (RSK-003, G-09).
Expected outcomes encode design intent, not measured behaviour. They are the specification the engine must satisfy.

benign.text: Your OTP is 452901 for your transaction of Rs 2,499.00. Never share this OTP with anyone. -Example Bank
benign.rationale: The single most important regression test in the corpus. This is a bank's own anti-fraud message. A naive keyword rule on 'OTP' flags it as CRITICAL. Flagging this actively harms users by training them to ignore warnings.

benign.text: Dear Customer, your KYC is due for periodic update. Please visit your nearest Example Bank branch or use the official Example Bank app. We will never ask for your PIN, OTP or password.
benign.rationale: Legitimate KYC communication. Banks DO legitimately mention KYC. The scam signal is a link or call demanding credentials — not the word KYC. Directing to a branch or official app is the opposite of the scam pattern.

benign.text: SCAM ALERT from Example Bank: Fraudsters may ask you to share your OTP, UPI PIN or CVV, or ask you to install AnyDesk to 'help' you. Example Bank will NEVER ask for these. Report fraud on our official helpline printed on your card.
benign.rationale: Adversarial-benign: a fraud-awareness broadcast that legitimately contains nearly every high-risk keyword in the rule set at once. Any engine that scores on keyword density will rate this CRITICAL. Requires directionality/negation handling.

benign.text: Rs 5,000.00 credited to your A/c XX4471 on 28-07-26 by UPI from RAHUL S. Ref 55XXXXXX2109. Not you? Call the number on your card.
benign.rationale: A genuine credit notification mentions credit and a UPI transfer but requests no action and asks for no credential. Distinguishes TL-PAY-001 (credential prompt framed as needed to receive) from an ordinary receipt.

benign.text: Your electricity bill of Rs 1,240 for July 2026 is due on 05-08-2026. Pay via the official Example Power app or your registered biller. Consumer no. 90XXXX21.
benign.rationale: Real utility bills exist. The scam marker in TL-UTIL-001 is a same-day disconnection threat plus an unofficial payment link — not the existence of a bill.

benign.text: Hi Priya, thanks for applying to Example Technologies. We would like to invite you to a first-round interview on 5 August at 11:00 IST. There is no fee at any stage of our hiring process. Reply to confirm.
benign.rationale: Legitimate recruitment. TL-JOB-001's verified basis (SRC-021) is 'never pay for job offers' — the signal is the payment demand, not the job offer.

benign.text: Your quarterly portfolio statement is available. Portfolio value Rs 2,14,300. Returns are subject to market risk. Example Securities is registered with SEBI, Reg. No. INZ0000XXXXX. Log in via our official website to view.
benign.rationale: A registered intermediary disclosing market risk is the inverse of TL-INV-001, whose verified basis (SRC-006, SRC-020) is a returns guarantee combined with risk denial. Risk disclosure should act as a negative indicator.

benign.text: hey, forgot my wallet at home again 😅 can you send me 300 for the cab? will return tonight
benign.rationale: People do genuinely ask friends for small amounts. TL-SOC-003's verified basis (SRC-021) concerns URGENT transfer requests warranting out-of-band verification. Absent urgency, pressure and a large amount, this is ordinary life.

benign.text: New login to WhatsApp Web from Chrome on Windows. If this was you, no action is needed. If not, log out of all devices from Settings > Linked Devices.
benign.rationale: A genuine device-linking notification mentions linked devices but requests nothing. TL-ATO-001's verified basis (SRC-017, SRC-016) is a request that the USER perform the linking under a false pretext.

benign.text: Your parcel BD90XXXX41 is out for delivery today and will arrive between 2pm and 6pm. Track it on the official Example Logistics app.
benign.rationale: Ordinary delivery notification. The courier pretext only becomes a signal when combined with a payment demand or a request to dial a USSD code.

benign.text: Hi team, great work this quarter. Please review the attached board deck before Friday's meeting. No payment or transfer is needed from anyone — just your feedback. Reach me on my usual desk extension.
benign.rationale: Near-miss for TL-AUTH-003: a genuine internal note from a manager with mild time pressure but NO impersonation cue and NO payment order. The boss-scam signal is executive/regulator impersonation PLUS an urgent transfer — not seniority alone.

benign.text: Security notice: a new device signed in to your exchange account. If this was you, no action is needed. If not, reset your password in the official app. We will never ask you to connect your wallet to 'verify' it.
benign.rationale: A genuine exchange security notice mentions wallets but requests no wallet connection and no action. TL-CRYP-001's signal is a wallet-connect request under a verification pretext — absent here.

benign.text: #CyberDost Alert from I4C/MHA: Fraudsters may ask you to install an APK, switch on Accessibility permission, or connect your crypto wallet at a 'verification' link. Official agencies will NEVER ask this. Never share your OTP. Report on 1930.
benign.rationale: Adversarial-benign: an official government awareness post that legitimately names every high-risk device/crypto action at once. A keyword or even a naive composite engine would flag it. The EDUCATIONAL_CONTENT suppressor must cancel TL-CRYP-001 and TL-MAL-002 even though their positive conditions are satisfied. This is the 'official educational/advisory language must be suppressible' requirement made into a test.

malicious.text: This is Inspector Sharma, CBI Cyber Crime Division. A parcel in your name containing illegal items has been seized and your Aadhaar is linked to a money laundering case. A warrant is issued. You are under digital arrest and must remain on this video call. Do NOT contact your family or any lawyer. To avoid immediate arrest, transfer Rs 85,000 as a refundable security deposit to the account provided for verification.
malicious.rationale: Contains every element of the modus operandi quoted verbatim in NITI Aayog SRC-012. The MVP demonstration scenario.

malicious.text: Your refund of Rs 8,750 is pending. To RECEIVE the amount, open your UPI app, scan the QR sent to you and enter your UPI PIN to confirm receipt. Refund expires in 30 minutes.
malicious.rationale: Directly contradicts CERT-In SRC-021: 'you don't need a UPI PIN or OTP to receive money'. The conjunction of receive-framing WITH a credential prompt is the high-confidence signal — neither element alone is sufficient.

malicious.text: Example Bank Security: unusual activity detected on your account. To stop the block, share the 6-digit OTP sent to your phone with our officer on this number immediately.
malicious.rationale: Contrast with B-001. Same keyword, opposite direction: this REQUESTS the OTP. Directionality is the discriminator.

malicious.text: Your card is due for re-verification. Confirm your 16-digit card number, expiry date and CVV at the secure link below within 24 hours to avoid suspension.
Hi! I'm running for a community award and need your vote. Please send me the 8-digit code you just received on WhatsApp so I can register your vote. It only takes a second!
malicious.rationale: Two independent verified sources describe this mechanism. Note the pretext is entirely benign-sounding — no threat, no payment, no urgency. Any engine keyed on fear or money misses it completely.

malicious.text: Hi, check this photo 😮 [link preview: 'Facebook — You were tagged in a photo'] Tap to verify your account and see who tagged you.
malicious.rationale: Matches CERT-In GhostPairing wording almost exactly, including the 'Hi, check this photo' teaser and Facebook-style preview.

malicious.text: JOIN OUR VIP TRADING GROUP 📈 Guaranteed 120% returns in 30 days. ZERO RISK. Our expert handles all trades for you — just deposit and watch your money grow. Only 5 seats left today!
malicious.rationale: '120% returns / zero risk' mirrors the exact fraud cue RBI's FAME booklet presents (SRC-020). 'Expert handles all trades' matches SEBI's malpractice description (SRC-006).

malicious.text: Congratulations! You are selected for an overseas job in Dubai, salary AED 9,000/month. To confirm your placement, pay the visa processing and documentation fee of Rs 18,500 today. Job guaranteed.
malicious.rationale: Directly contradicts CERT-In SRC-021: 'Never pay for job offers.' Contrast with B-006, which explicitly states no fee.

malicious.text: Beta, this is your uncle. I've lost my phone and this is my new number. I'm at the hospital and need Rs 45,000 urgently for the admission deposit. Please transfer to this UPI ID now, I'll explain later. Don't call, I can't talk here.
malicious.rationale: SRC-021 prescribes verifying by calling directly — this message pre-empts exactly that check ('Don't call'), which is itself the strongest signal. Contrast with B-008.

malicious.text: Hey! It's me, I made a new account because my old one got hacked. I'm stuck and need Rs 12,000 sent to this UPI right now. Please don't tell anyone, it's embarrassing.
Example Bank: Your account will be BLOCKED today. Complete your KYC immediately at http://examplebank-kyc-verify.example/update and enter your registered mobile, card number and OTP to reactivate.
malicious.rationale: The full KYC attack chain from RP p.12: pretext → link → credential request. Contrast with B-002, which shares the KYC pretext and nothing else.

malicious.text: This is your CEO. I'm in a board meeting and cannot take calls. I need you to urgently transfer Rs 4,50,000 to a vendor account I'll send now to close a deal. Keep this strictly confidential until it's done.
malicious.rationale: Boss-scam pattern verified by PIB/MHA (SRC-022, MR-EVID-004): senior-identity claim + urgent transfer + secrecy, over a messaging app. Contrast with B-011, which has seniority and urgency but no payment order.

malicious.text: Your crypto airdrop is ready to claim! Verify your holdings at trust-wallet-verify.example and connect your wallet to confirm ownership. Continue with our agent on Telegram to release the funds.
malicious.rationale: Matches the I4C CyberDost Trust Wallet chain (SRC-024, MR-EVID-010): fake verification site + wallet-connect request + off-platform handoff. Contrast with B-012, which mentions wallets but requests no connection.

malicious.text: URGENT: Your SIM will be deactivated today due to incomplete verification. To keep your number active, dial *401*98765XXXXX# immediately from your phone. Act now to avoid disconnection.
malicious.rationale: The narrowed TL-TEL-001: a pressured request to dial a call-forwarding/USSD code, verified by I4C CyberDost (SRC-013, MR-EVID-008). Note there is NO courier pretext — that clause was removed as unsupported. Contrast with B-010, which is a plain delivery notice with no code to dial.

ambiguous.text: Important update regarding your account: http://exmpl.co/x9k2
ambiguous.rationale: One weak indicator and no context. RP p.13 is explicit that a single weak signal must not suffice. Must return INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with an explanation of what is missing — never 'safe'.

ambiguous.text: Dear customer, please verify your account details at your earliest convenience to avoid service interruption.
ambiguous.rationale: Authority-ish framing and mild urgency, but no credential request, no link, no payment demand. RP p.13 classifies authority claims WITHOUT a payment step as medium-suspicion needing corroboration.

ambiguous.text: Our fund has averaged 18% annually over the last three years. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Interested in learning more?
ambiguous.rationale: Tests the boundary of TL-INV-001. A historical return figure WITH a risk disclosure is not a guarantee. Registration status is unknown, so it cannot be cleared either. Genuine uncertainty — route to review.

ambiguous.text: Your application has moved to the next stage. Please complete the onboarding formalities on our portal to proceed.
ambiguous.rationale: 'Onboarding formalities' may or may not conceal a fee demand. TL-JOB-001's verified basis is specifically a PAYMENT requirement, which is absent here.

ambiguous.text: Scan this QR to complete the transaction. [image attached]
ambiguous.rationale: No receive/refund framing, so TL-PAY-002 does not fire; payee identity is unresolvable from the artifact, so TL-PAY-003 is DEFERRED (CONF-003). Correct behaviour is to surface CERT-In SRC-021's guidance — verify the payee's banking name — as a recommendation, not a finding.

ambiguous.text: Aapka account block ho jayega. Turant KYC update karne ke liye OTP bhejo warna account band ho jayega.
ambiguous.rationale: A transliterated Hinglish message that is unambiguously malicious to a human reader (KYC pretext + account-block threat + OTP request), but which the English-only knowledge base CANNOT detect (G-08, CONF-004). Expected behaviour is an EXPLICIT unsupported-language flag per NFR-009 — never a silent low score that reads as 'safe'. This case exists to make the multilingual gap visible and testable rather than theoretical.
